 “ The Body ,” a teen psychological drama created by Quinn Shephard, debuted as the No. 3 TV title on Netflix for the week of Nov. 9-16. The series premiered on Nov. 11, and in its first five days of streaming it reached 5.1 million views.
 Two TV titles outranked it: docuseries “Taken: Natalee Holloway” with 7.2 million views in its second week on the chart, and Season 2 of “Black Doves” with 6.6 million, also making its second chart appearance. The new “Black Doves” episodes also drove viewers back towards Season 1, which landed in fifth place with 3.7 million views. Ahead of it at No. 4 was “Doozie’s Doghouse,” a new children’s series, with 5 million views in four days.

 “Power,” the popular Starz series that debuted in 2014, had its Netflix debut on Nov. 9 and became the sixth title on the chart with 2.9 million views. With 2.4 million views apiece, sixth and seventh place went to the Nov. 9 edition of “Raw: 2026” and Season 3 of “Nobody Wants This,” which is in its fourth chart week. Docuseries “The One About Matthew Perry” landed in ninth place with 1.7 million views in its third chart week, and the last spot on the chart went to Season 2 of kids’ series “Danny Go!” with 1.5 million views in its fifth week.
 Also of note on this week’s Netflix Top 10 was the movie “Heartland” starring Jessica Chastain, which hit 7.3 million views in its first three days of streaming.
